hints.title: IPv4 Validation Invariant
hints.text: A valid IPv4 address contains exactly four octets between 0 and 255 without leading zeros.

hints.title: Anchored Regex Pattern
hints.text: Construct an anchored regular expression matching the structure of valid octets joined by dots.

hints.title: Aggregation and Ordering
hints.text: Filter records that do not match the valid expression, count occurrences per IP, and sort in descending order.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT ip, COUNT(*) AS invalid_count
FROM logs
WHERE ip NOT REGEXP '^((25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9][0-9]|[0-9])\\.){3}(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9][0-9]|[0-9])$'
GROUP BY ip
ORDER BY invalid_count DESC, ip DESC;
```

variables: n: number of rows in logs table
complexity.notes: Matches regular expressions during table scan and aggregates resulting invalid IPs with sorting.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Custom string splits without full regex validation miss leading zeros or range bounds.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouping buffer stores distinct invalid IP counts.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Constructs valid IPv4 regex ensuring octet bounds and absence of leading zeros.

solutions.code:
SELECT ip, COUNT(*) AS invalid_count
FROM logs
WHERE ip NOT REGEXP '^((25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9][0-9]|[0-9])\\.){3}(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9][0-9]|[0-9])$'
GROUP BY ip
ORDER BY invalid_count DESC, ip DESC;

SELECT ip, COUNT(*) AS invalid_count
FROM logs
WHERE ip !~ '^((25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9][0-9]|[0-9])\x2E){3}(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9][0-9]|[0-9])$'
GROUP BY ip
ORDER BY invalid_count DESC, ip DESC;
